answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks through hardware attestation. Agents execute within trusted enclaves, signing heartbeats with an onyx chip. The network checks each signature against a strict latency delta, forcing an attacker to incur the verifiable capital cost of buying dedicated silicon per identity. This creates a steep cost mesa that blocks cheap virtualization. However, this architecture depends on centralized vendors and remains susceptible to hardware side-channel leaks.
